entry.title: Silent Payments for Electrum
entry.summary:
A new tool has been introduced to enhance the use of Silent Payments, complementing an existing sending plugin that was previously released on the Electrum plugins registry. The latest addition, spscand, serves as a scanner specifically designed for Silent Payments and integrates seamlessly with the aforementioned plugin. The project is open source and available under the MIT license at [ZenulAbidin/spscand](https://github.com/ZenulAbidin/spscand) on GitHub. The most recent release, version v0.1.1, comes GPG-signed, providing users with additional confidence in its authenticity and integrity.
spscand operates by identifying payments made to sp1 addresses (BIP352 1.1.2), closely monitoring their subsequent spends and blockchain reorganizations. It communicates findings through both a local JSON API and webhook notifications, allowing for flexible integration into various workflows or monitoring setups. Notably, the tool is engineered with privacy in mind; it does not query any external server regarding specific addresses, outputs, or transactions. Instead, block data can be sourced from a personal node, a blindbit server, or by utilizing BIP352 filters, ensuring user autonomy and confidentiality throughout the scanning process. Additionally, Tor support is included, further bolstering the privacy features of the solution.
With this new development, users now have access to a comprehensive toolkit for managing Silent Payments—from sending transactions to efficiently monitoring and tracking them—while maintaining a strong emphasis on security and privacy. Feedback and constructive critique are actively encouraged to support ongoing improvements and refinement of the tool.
